chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Amr al-Tabib, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.

Concerning a man who ruptured a slave-girl with his finger and tore her bladder so that she could not control her urine: he assigned for her one-third of the diyah, one hundred and sixty-six dinars and two-thirds of a dinar, and he ruled that he was liable to her for the dowry equivalent of the women of her people.

key_terms.بَوْلَهَا: her urine; here meaning urinary control
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dinar, a gold coin used as a legal measure of compensation
key_terms.صَدَاقِ مِثْلِ: the dowry equivalent customarily given to similar women

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man injures a slave-girl and causes her to lose control of her urine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury inflicted upon a slave-girl, specifically when the injury causes permanent loss of urinary control. It specifies financial compensation as one-third of the diyah along with mahr al-mithl, showing the detailed treatment of bodily harm and compensatory liability in Shia fiqh.
